I am an old man now, 84 years, and I have been planting maize on this land in Iringa for many seasons. I do not have money for chemical fertilizer — those sacks from the shop are too expensive for me, so I use the manure from my few cattle and goats to put on this plot. I keep my own seed from last harvest like my father taught me, and I plant beans together with the maize so the soil stays strong. My sons and grandchildren help me in the field because my back is not strong anymore, and when the weeding is heavy I pay a few young men from the village to help for some days.
